sources.title: London Strategic Infrastructure Requirements
sources.verified_claim: City Hall's strategic infrastructure work covers rail, road, electricity, heat, waste, water, flood risk, digital and green infrastructure and links infrastructure planning/funding status to housing and economic growth.

sources.title: Climate change and weather
sources.verified_claim: City Hall expects hotter, drier summers and wetter winters with more intense rainfall, and identifies flood, drought and heat adaptation measures; this is regional trend evidence, not parcel-specific risk.

sources.title: London City Resilience Strategy
sources.verified_claim: The City Resilience Strategy addresses long-term stresses including climate and extreme-weather impacts and sets collaborative mitigation projects; it provides governance context rather than development permission.

sources.title: ADD2808 Reducing disruption caused by infrastructure delivery
sources.verified_claim: City Hall approved £294,483 of Regulators' Pioneer Fund support to reduce disruption from infrastructure delivery under the Upgrading London's Infrastructure programme; programme funding is system-level, not parcel funding.

sources.title: Thames Barrier
sources.verified_claim: The Mayor stated options for the Thames Barrier after the 2040 decision point remain open and highlighted the need for full funding and nationally significant infrastructure recognition; this is long-term regional flood-defence context.

sources.title: London Councils and Mayor unveil new London Infrastructure Framework to drive growth
sources.verified_claim: London Councils describes the Infrastructure Framework as a joint long-term plan covering transport, energy, water, wastewater, flood protection and digital connectivity to enable housing, jobs and resilience.

sources.title: Notice of intention to commence Local Plan
sources.verified_claim: Lambeth formally published notice that it intends to prepare the Lambeth Local Plan 2029, with preparation expected to begin 31 October 2026; commencement is not a site allocation or planning permission.

sources.title: Mayor invests £4.6 million to boost London's green and blue spaces and build a more climate resilient city
sources.verified_claim: City Hall announced £4.6 million for green and blue infrastructure, including £3.5 million to 33 projects and £1.1 million for a tree-equity project; awards demonstrate delivery capacity but do not identify funding for the three sample parcels.
